newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 7.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters on Thursday called for northern tribes to take a harder line against protesters before official commemorations could return to Waitangi. Speaking after protesters had removed the New Zealand flag from the flagpole on the Waitangi Treaty grounds and replaced it with flags of their own, he said Nga Puhi had put up with their protocols being trampled for too long. Such behaviour would not be tolerated on other maraes. Page 1.

Aotearoa Television Network did not approve spending on clothes by directors Tukuroirangi Morgan and Morehu McDonald, company officials said on Thursday. Morgan, now a NZ First MP, and McDonald spent a reported $16,000 of Aotearoa Television money at an upmarket men's clothing store last year. Two weeks before the election Morgan spent $4000 on clothes, including an $89 pair of underpants. Page 1.

Maori disadvantages must be addressed, Prime Minister Jim Bolger and Governor-General Sir Michael Hardie Boys said at Waitangi Day commemorations in Wellington on Thursday. The low-key garden party at Government House was attended by about 750 guests, including Prince Michael of Kent. Bolger said the coalition agreement emphasised the government's commitment to work with Maoridom to achieve their full participation in society. Page 2.

Police officers no longer support a comprehensive strategic plan developed five years ago to map the future direction of police. The Police Association last week told Police Minister Jack Elder that the strategy, known as Policing 2000, was theoretical and did not reflect the realities of frontline policing. Page 2.

Prime Minister Jim Bolger meets his Australian counterpart next week and is expected to raise an Australian proposal to make New Zealanders living there wait two years before they can claim welfare benefits. At present, New Zealanders living in Australia can claim benefits after six months. Australians living in New Zealand do the same under a reciprocal agreement. Page 2.

The government had ignored much of its constitutional responsibilities to the Treaty of Waitangi, former governor-general Sir Paul Reeves said on Thursday. Speaking at the Waitangi Day commemorations at the Onuku Marae near Akaroa, Sir Paul said Maoris had been dissatisfied with the representation system from the beginning. Page 2.

New Zealand wine producers would have to raise exports by about 30 percent to accommodate increased production by the year 2000, New Zealand Wine Guild deputy chairman Andrew Hendry said on Thursday. With more land being turned over to wine production in New Zealand, and increased output by new winemakers, new Zealand's total production is set to grow significantly over the next few years. Page 13.

Oil giant Fletcher Challenge Energy is restructuring all of its New Zealand operations, starting at the top. Management will be the focus of the first phase of the comprehensive review which started this week and is due to take about a month. Stage two will concentrate on the operational side of New Zealand's largest energy company. Page 13.

Reserves in the New Zealand Oil and Gas share of the Kupe oil project may be larger than previously thought. In a progress report for the fourth quarter of 1996, NZOG said continuing interpretation of a major three-dimensional seismic programme was likely to result in revised reserve estimates. Page 14.
